mechanism_narrative: The steady week-over-week rise in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicates recovering daytime circulation, which should continue to lift retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks as commuting-linked discretionary trips rebuild.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to the prior 4-week mean even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both increase for at least two more consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL stays elevated while WORKPLACES remains depressed, more activity is occurring near home rather than in shopping districts, so RETAIL_REC should fall over the next four weeks as out-of-home retail trips are displaced.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 8 points while WORKPLACES stays below -30 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated and WORKPLACES remains below -30 for the next month.

mechanism_narrative: The continued improvement in GROCERY_PHARM while RETAIL_REC remains far below baseline implies substitution toward necessity trips, which should keep RETAIL_REC lower over the next one to two weeks as consumers prioritize essential shopping over discretionary retail.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases for two straight weeks while GROCERY_PHARM stays positive and RETAIL_REC remains at least 20 points below baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in TRANSIT below the recent trend signals renewed friction in public movement, and retail visits should weaken within two weeks because fewer corridor trips and fewer transfer-linked errands reach shopping areas.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -25 points after being above -25 in the prior week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within two weeks after TRANSIT crosses below -25 points from above.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in PARKS and fall in WORKPLACES indicates a leisure-oriented weekly pattern, and that pattern should reduce retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks because outdoor substitute activities crowd out shopping-center visits.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while PARKS stays weakly negative and WORKPLACES does not fall further.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM turns positive and RESIDENTIAL softens, households are resuming routine errand chains outside the home, so RETAIL_REC should improve over the next two weeks through spillover from renewed low-risk out-of-home movement.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM crosses above 0 while RESIDENTIAL declines below 9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks after GROCERY_PHARM becomes positive and RESIDENTIAL drops below 9.

mechanism_narrative: If both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES continue improving together, that joint easing of mobility constraints should accelerate discretionary shopping trips, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks than it was in the prior month.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over 28 days despite two consecutive weekly gains in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: In a near-normal mobility regime, the gradual narrowing of the gap between RESIDENTIAL and WORKPLACES should translate into more mixed-purpose outings and a modest retail recovery over the next one week, because people spend less time confined at home.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not tick up within one week even though RESIDENTIAL stays elevated and WORKPLACES remains negative.
